# Excellence 2026: Performance & Innovation Solutions


October 29, 2026


by Craig Patton


##


Innovation in government should drive performance. As public-sector organizations respond to changing community needs, workforce pressures, and growing service expectations, technology can help them rethink established processes and find better ways to deliver on their missions.


That can mean making faster, more informed decisions, redesigning workflows, improving access to services, or using resources more effectively. Impactful innovations connect new approaches with measurable improvements, helping organizations perform better while delivering greater value to the communities they serve.


## Celebrating Excellence in Performance & Innovation Solutions


The[Tyler Excellence Awards](https://www.tylertech.com/about-us/tyler-client-difference/tyler-excellence-awards) recognize organizations putting those ideas into practice. As 2026 winds down, we’re highlighting four Performance & Innovation winners, organizations using Tyler solutions to rethink processes, strengthen accountability, and achieve meaningful results for their organizations and communities.


## Adapting Dispatch to Improve Emergency Response


As call volumes increased and staffing models evolved, the Public Safety Communications Center in[Scarborough, Maine](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/blog-articles/smarter-dispatching-for-scarborough-fire-response) , needed a more reliable way to manage complex fire response plans. Using Enterprise Public Safety, they have:


- Helped resolve staffing issues, allowing more time to be spent on people vs. systems
- Improved response accuracy, consistency, and dispatch reliability
- Increased better data-driven decisions fueled by analytics that provide mission-critical insights


“The system removes a lot of the guesswork,” said Emergency Communications Manager Joseph Thornton. “Dispatchers can trust that the run cards reflect what resources are actually available at that moment.”


## Modernizing Records Management for Greater Efficiency and Convenience


To improve efficiency and strengthen service across their geographically large, rural community, the[Yavapai County, Arizona](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/case-studies/unlocking-efficiency-and-resident-convenience) , Recorder’s Office added Recording Access and a scan-first process to enhance its Enterprise Records Management solution. These enhancements:


- Reduced postage costs and the risk of document loss
- Streamlined staff workflows
- Limited the need for residents to travel long distances to record documents


“I just spoke with a gentleman who came in to record a document and was amazed he’d get it back the same day,” said County Recorder Michelle Burchill. “Moments like that really stick with us. The feedback from the community has been fantastic with lots of surprised, happy faces.”


## Connecting Communications With Service Delivery


The city of[Buckeye, Arizona](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/case-studies/connecting-permitting-processes-with-resident-communications) , sought better ways to send email, text, and call reminders to residents. The city implemented Notify to address communication gaps and support business processes across departments. Using Notify, they:


- Filled communications gaps for existing software
- Enabled email, text, and call reminders for various city needs
- Supported Utility Billing and city clerk passport appointment notifications
- Augmented existing software and business processes


“It’s better engagement with the community,” said Julian Garcia, IT applications manager.


## Transforming Transportation to Strengthen District Resources


After identifying inefficiencies and missed subsidy opportunities,[Allentown School District in Pennsylvania](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/case-studies/urban-district-unlocks-millions-in-transportation-funding) brought bus routing in-house and implemented Tyler’s Student Transportation software to align transportation performance to state funding requirements. Since adopting the solution, the district has:


- Projected $2 million more in state subsidy to strengthen district funding
- Optimized tiered routes to maximize mileage and bus capacity
- Fine-tuned routes and schedules for real-world traffic challenges


“Getting half of what we spend on transportation back in state subsidy is a great thing,” said Andrew Krahulik-Knapp, director of transportation. “It helps put the money back in the classrooms.”
